issues.failure_explanation: Assumption 2.1(ii) and Assumption 2.2(i) require uniform ellipticity, i.e. sigma sigma^T >= kappa I for all x in R^d. For the geometric Brownian motion sigma(x)=sigma*diag(x^1,...,x^d), the smallest eigenvalue of sigma sigma^T is sigma^2 min_i (x^i)^2. It tends to 0 as any coordinate goes to 0 and equals 0 on the coordinate hyperplanes. So the stated assumptions fail for the paper's only concrete example (and for the 1-D game put used in Section 5). The claim that the example is 'straightforward to check' is false.

failure_location.quote: it is straightforward to check that Assumptions~\ref{assumptions} and \ref{assumptionpde} hold

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State honestly that the example violates uniform ellipticity. Either localize or regularize the model (e.g. work on a region away from the boundary, or truncate the volatility) with a short argument that the assumptions and results still apply, or relax the ellipticity assumption where it is actually used.
issues.overall_effect: The paper does not show that its theory (existence/PDE representation under ellipticity, penalty bound, local-time bounds) covers the basket game put or the Black–Scholes experiment it uses as motivation and validation.
issues.title: Black–Scholes example claimed to satisfy the standing assumptions although uniform ellipticity fails
issues.why_classification: The theorems themselves are untouched, but the demonstration of applicability fails. A contained localization or relaxation argument, or a weakened claim, is needed, so this is more than a one-line fix but needs no new global architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Applying Ekeland's variational principle \citep{Ekeland1974} to the continuous function \(-\ell\) on the complete metric space \(K\)

issues.failure_explanation: Ekeland's principle gives a point where l(t,x) - (eta/delta)*d((t,x),(t_eta,x_eta)) <= l(t_eta,x_eta) for all (t,x), with a perturbation linear in the distance. This is not the quadratic perturbation (eta/delta)*d^2 used in l_eta. Near the point d^2 <= d, so maximality of l - (eta/delta)d does not imply maximality of l - (eta/delta)d^2; the inference goes the wrong way. The linear perturbation is not C^{1,2} at the point, so it cannot serve as a test function. The claims that rho_eta has zero gradient and L rho_eta >= 0 and that the viscosity supersolution inequality applies are therefore unsupported. Case 2 is essential because maximizers can lie on the kink set Gamma (e.g. the put kink). Also, neither case shows that a positive maximizer cannot sit at t=T; this needs p_b(T,.)<=g.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Case 2 by a valid argument for non-smooth obstacles: use a smooth variational principle (Borwein–Preiss), or a standard perturbed-test-function or doubling-variables argument, so that the penalization is C^{1,2} and its Hessian is controlled. Add the one-line check that a positive maximizer cannot occur at t=T. The statements are expected to survive unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition apb1 is the source of the one-sided penalty bounds lambda(Y-p_b)^- <= 2D_b^- and lambda(p_w-Y)^- <= 2D_w^+. These feed the O(1/lambda) penalty error, the a priori estimates, and all discretization bounds. Their rigorous proof is incomplete whenever maximizers can lie on Gamma.
issues.title: Ekeland's variational principle misapplied in Case 2 of the penalty-comparison proposition
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is plausible and a known technique should repair it, but the repair is a contained new argument rather than a typo fix. Because the gap is in the proposition itself, it propagates to the downstream results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, $\|Y^\lambda\|^p_{\mathbb{S}^p}<C_2$ follows from induction, the Lipschitz property of $\bar{g}$, and \eqref{xbound}.

issues.failure_explanation: For p>2 the proof passes through E∫|Z_s|^p ds (and E|Z_s|^p inside the integral) and then bounds it by (1/N)||Z||^p_{H^p}, where ||Z||^p_{H^p}=E(∫|Z|^2)^{p/2}. E∫|Z|^p ds is not controlled by that norm, so the step as written is invalid. The correct route needs Hölder before taking expectations, (∫|Z|ds)^p <= (τ-t)^{p/2}(∫|Z|^2)^{p/2}, giving a factor N^{-p/2}. The line dropping the penalty term lambda(...)^- treats it as 0 although it is only bounded by a constant (Corollary stoapb). Gronwall is then applied without that additive constant. The proof also refers to an undefined 'Lipschitz property of \bar{g}'.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the estimate with Hölder applied to (∫|f|ds)^p, keep the bounded penalty contribution as an additive constant, and use g Lipschitz with the moment bound on X. This is a routine local repair and the statement is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The lambda-independent bound ||Y^lambda||_{S^p}+||Z^lambda||_{H^p} <= C_2 is not rigorously derived as written. It is used in the discretization-error and Z-independent analyses.
issues.title: A priori estimate proof bounds the driver's Z-term by an invalid H^p-type quantity and drops the penalty term
issues.why_classification: The result is standard and a short local correction restores it with no change to the statement, rate, or method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \(\lambda\asymp \Delta t^{-1/2}\) yields the rate \(O(\Delta t^{1/4})\) for the value process.

issues.failure_explanation: The proved bound is C(lambda*Delta t^{1/2}+1/lambda). With lambda=Delta t^{-1/2} the first term equals 1, so the bound does not tend to 0 and gives no rate. The terms balance at lambda ≍ Delta t^{-1/4}, which yields Delta t^{1/4}. The claimed choice therefore contradicts the paper's own corollary, both in the Introduction and in Section 4.

failure_location.quote: In particular, if $\lambda=\Delta t^{-\frac{1}{2}}$, we obtain the minimal error rate

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace lambda ≍ Delta t^{-1/2} by lambda ≍ Delta t^{-1/4} in the Z-dependent discussion (Introduction and Section 4), keeping the Delta t^{1/4} rate. Also fix the stray lambda=Delta t^{1/2} in the Z-independent paragraph.
issues.overall_effect: The tuning rule for the Z-dependent (general Lipschitz) case is wrong as stated; the Delta t^{1/4} rate itself is still obtainable with a different lambda.
issues.title: Wrong balancing choice of lambda for the Y-rate in the Z-dependent bound
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the exponent preserves the stated rate and all formal results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: it indicates that the experiment remains in a pre-asymptotic regime
This behavior does not contradict the theory.

issues.failure_explanation: In the penalty sweep at n=200 the estimate is already essentially constant from lambda about 2e3 to 3.2e12 (abs. error 4.45e-2 down to 4.149e-2). Hence in the grid sweep, where lambda >= 1e4, the penalty contribution is negligible and the measured error is dominated by time discretization/regression. The sweep does not test the coupled bound with its lambda-dependent terms lambda*Delta t and lambda*Delta t~ (with exact forward sampling, m does not appear). Over six orders of magnitude of lambda*Delta t (up to ~1.6e10) no growth appears, so 'pre-asymptotic' is not supported. The data simply do not exhibit the lambda*Delta t term of the upper bound. The grid errors also deviate from the fitted C n^{-1/2} (about 28% and 39% below the fit at n=800 and 1600, and a decay ratio of only 1.14 from n=1600 to 3200). No seed variability is reported.

failure_location.quote: This behavior is fully consistent with the theoretical \(O(n^{-1/2})\) prediction.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the numerical claims: the experiments show only that the discretization error decays at a roughly n^{-1/2} rate with a negligible penalty error. They do not validate the lambda-coupling or the two-grid terms. Optionally add experiments with a coarse forward grid, smaller lambda, or reported seed variability.
issues.overall_effect: The statements that the experiments 'support' the two-grid error analysis and the lambda≍n^{1/2} balancing overstate what the numerics show. They provide no evidence for the amplification mechanism or the coupling rule.
issues.title: Numerical section claims confirmation of the coupled error bound and a 'pre-asymptotic' regime that the data do not support
issues.why_classification: No theorem is affected; the fix is to weaken the prose claims so the paper's claims match what the data show.
